representation.shell_command:
python3 -c "
sel={('B','1'),('B','2'),('B','82'),('B','143'),('D','1'),('D','2'),('D','82'),('D','143')}
p=[[],[],[]]
a=[[],[],[]]
for line in open('$(inputs.pdb.path)'):
    if line.startswith('ATOM'):
        ch=line[21]
        rs=line[22:26].strip()
        xyz=(float(line[30:38]),float(line[38:46]),float(line[46:54]))
        for i in range(3): a[i].append(xyz[i])
        if (ch,rs) in sel:
            for i in range(3): p[i].append(xyz[i])
o=open('box_params.tsv','w')
o.write('metric\tx\ty\tz\tn_atoms\n')
o.write('protein_centroid\t%.3f\t%.3f\t%.3f\t%d\n'%(sum(a[0])/len(a[0]),sum(a[1])/len(a[1]),sum(a[2])/len(a[2]),len(a[0])))
o.write('protein_min\t%.3f\t%.3f\t%.3f\t-\n'%(min(a[0]),min(a[1]),min(a[2])))
o.write('protein_max\t%.3f\t%.3f\t%.3f\t-\n'%(max(a[0]),max(a[1]),max(a[2])))
o.write('bpg_pocket_centroid\t%.3f\t%.3f\t%.3f\t%d\n'%(sum(p[0])/len(p[0]),sum(p[1])/len(p[1]),sum(p[2])/len(p[2]),len(p[0])))
o.write('bpg_pocket_min\t%.3f\t%.3f\t%.3f\t-\n'%(min(p[0]),min(p[1]),min(p[2])))
o.write('bpg_pocket_max\t%.3f\t%.3f\t%.3f\t-\n'%(max(p[0]),max(p[1]),max(p[2])))
o.close()
"

**Inputs**
- Receptor: RCSB **2HHB** (deoxyhaemoglobin, human, T state, 1.74 Å) → `Prepare receptor` v1.5.7 (AutoDockTools `prepare_receptor4`, polar H added, non-polar H/lone pairs merged) → 5,737-atom PDBQT
- Ligand: aspirin, **PubChem CID 2244**, 3D conformer; protonated by Open Babel at **pH 7.4**, so it docks as the carboxylate anion
- Box: `Calculate the box parameters using RDKit` on 2HHB gave the tetramer bounding box 73.7 × 61.1 × 64.8 Å centred at **(11.23, 13.30, 40.58)**

**Results — AutoDock Vina 1.2.3, `vina` scoring, seed 42**

| Run | Box | Exh. | Best affinity | Spread of reported modes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| β-cleft / 2,3-BPG cavity (job `…1250c470`) | 26 Å cube at tetramer centre | 32 | **−4.976 kcal/mol** | −4.98 → −4.62 (9 modes) |
| Blind, whole tetramer (job `…1dcba05f`) | 76 × 64 × 68 Å | 16 | **−4.953 kcal/mol** | −4.95 → −4.16 (20 modes) |

Converting the best score with ΔG = −RT ln(1/K_d) at 298 K (my own arithmetic, RT = 0.592 kcal/mol) gives **K_d ≈ 2×10⁻⁴ M, i.e. roughly 200–240 µM**.

**How to read this — the number matters less than the pattern.** The blind search found nothing better anywhere on the tetramer than the central cavity did, and in *both* runs poses separated by 10–29 Å score within 0.3–0.8 kcal/mol of the best one. That degeneracy is the classic signature of a ligand with no real binding pocket: aspirin is just making generic surface contacts. There is no discriminating site.

**Caveats, in order of importance**
1. **This is the wrong physics for aspirin–haemoglobin.** Aspirin's real interaction with HbA is *covalent acetylation* of lysine side chains (irreversible acetyl transfer), which docking cannot model at all. 3. Rigid receptor, no explicit waters, deoxy (T-state) conformer only — the BPG cleft is conformation-dependent and R-state Hb would differ.
4. I did **not** verify whether `prepare_receptor4` retained the four HEM groups in the PDBQT (atom count is ambiguous). It doesn't affect this conclusion — the top poses are in the central cavity, far from the haems — and Vina has no proper Fe parameters in any case.

- β-cleft/2,3-BPG cavity box: −4.976 kcal/mol
- Blind whole-tetramer box: −4.953 kcal/mol (no better site found)

Both jobs finished. Both docked-pose collections are `populated_state: ok` with one SDF of ranked poses each. Here is the complete result.

## What was run

All work was done on **usegalaxy.org** (Galaxy 26.2), history `bbd44e69cb8906b557ef1bf7c4102fde`.

**Inputs**
- **Receptor:** RCSB **2HHB** — human deoxyhaemoglobin, T state, 1.74 Å (Fermi, Perutz, Shaanan & Fourme), fetched from `files.rcsb.org`. Prepared with `Prepare receptor` v1.5.7 (AutoDockTools `prepare_receptor4`: polar hydrogens added, non-polar H and lone pairs merged) → 5,737-atom PDBQT (dataset `f9cad7b01a47213573ec34771735a93b`, job `…1dbbf17`).
- **Ligand:** aspirin, **PubChem CID 2244**, 3D conformer via PUG-REST. Open Babel protonated it at **pH 7.4**, so it docks as the carboxylate **anion** — the correct physiological species.
- **Box:** `Calculate the box parameters using RDKit` v2021.03.5 on 2HHB returned the tetramer bounding box **73.70 × 61.12 × 64.79 Å, centred at (11.2295, 13.297, 40.5835)** (job `…1d8793b`). For a haemoglobin tetramer that centre lies in the central water cavity on the molecular dyad — the 2,3-BPG / allosteric-effector cleft lined by Val1β, His2β, Lys82β and His143β, which is the literature-supported site for salicylate-type ligands and the Lys82β acetylation target.

**Dockings — AutoDock Vina 1.2.3, `vina` scoring function, random seed 42**

| Run | Box | Exh. | Best affinity | Reported mode range |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| β-cleft / central cavity (job `bbd44e69cb8906b5f2e303191250c470`) | 26 × 26 × 26 Å at (11.23, 13.30, 40.58) | 32 | **−4.976 kcal/mol** | −4.976 → −4.616 (9 modes) |
| Blind, whole tetramer (job `bbd44e69cb8906b5226db4e81dcba05f`) | 76 × 64 × 68 Å, same centre | 16 | **−4.953 kcal/mol** | −4.953 → −4.159 (20 modes) |

Vina's decomposition of the best focused pose: intermolecular −5.793, ligand internal −0.415, torsional penalty +0.873, unbound reference −0.359 → **−4.976 kcal/mol**.

Converting the best score via ΔG = −RT·ln(1/K_d) at 298 K (my own arithmetic, RT = 0.592 kcal/mol) gives **K_d ≈ 2.3 × 10⁻⁴ M**, i.e. roughly **200–240 µM** across the two runs.

## How to read this

The pattern matters more than the number, and it is unambiguous:

- The **blind search over the entire tetramer found nothing better** than the focused central-cavity box (−4.95 vs −4.98 kcal/mol). So the focused box did not miss a superior site.
- In **both** runs, poses separated by large distances score almost identically — in the focused run modes 5–8 sit 10–14 Å from the top pose yet within 0.3 kcal/mol of it; in the blind run modes 4, 10, 15 and 17 sit **25–29 Å** away and are within 0.6–0.7 kcal/mol.

That degeneracy is the classic signature of a ligand with **no real binding pocket**. Aspirin is making generic surface contacts; there is no discriminating site on 2HHB.

## Caveats, in order of importance

1. **This is arguably the wrong physics for aspirin–haemoglobin.** Aspirin's biologically meaningful interaction with HbA is *covalent acetylation* of lysine side chains (irreversible acetyl transfer, e.g. Lys82β in this very cavity), which docking cannot model at all. The −5 kcal/mol here describes only the weak **reversible pre-association** — which is consistent with the fact that acetylation requires prolonged exposure rather than tight binding.
2. **Vina scores carry an RMSE of roughly 2–2.5 kcal/mol** against measured affinities. Treat this as order-of-magnitude ("weak, high-micromolar to millimolar"), not a measurement. This is a prediction, not a lookup, and Vina reports no per-pose confidence metric beyond the score itself.
3. **Rigid receptor, no explicit waters, deoxy (T) state only.** The BPG cleft is strongly conformation-dependent; R-state (oxy) haemoglobin would give different numbers.
4. I did **not** verify whether `prepare_receptor4` retained the four HEM groups — the 5,737 atom count is ambiguous between protein-only and protein-plus-haem. It does not affect this conclusion: the top poses are in the central cavity, far from the haems, and Vina has no proper Fe parameters in any case.
5. The blind run emitted Vina's expected `WARNING: Search space volume is greater than 27000 Angstrom^3`. Large-box searches are less reliable per-pose, which is exactly why it was run as a cross-check on the focused box rather than as the primary result.

## ANSWER

**Predicted affinity: −4.98 kcal/mol** (AutoDock Vina 1.2.3, best pose), corresponding to **K_d ≈ 200–240 µM**.

- β-cleft / 2,3-BPG central cavity: **−4.976 kcal/mol**
- Blind whole-tetramer search: **−4.953 kcal/mol** (no better site found anywhere)

Aspirin binds haemoglobin **weakly and non-specifically** — poses up to 29 Å apart score within <1 kcal/mol of the best, so 2HHB has no genuine aspirin pocket. Note that aspirin's real interaction with Hb is covalent lysine acetylation, which docking cannot represent.

Provenance: usegalaxy.org history `bbd44e69cb8906b557ef1bf7c4102fde`; Vina jobs `bbd44e69cb8906b5f2e303191250c470` (focused) and `bbd44e69cb8906b5226db4e81dcba05f` (blind), both `state: ok`, `exit_code: 0`; receptor RCSB **2HHB**; ligand PubChem **CID 2244**.
